person.name: Ramana Tata
person.text: Streak and his LinkedIn headline give **Global Sourcing, Procurement & Logistics Lead**. A public org chart (TheOrg, marked unverified) lists him as **Sourcing – Procurement – Logistics Specialist at Taro Pharmaceuticals Canada since September 2021**, based in **Toronto**, on a small 2-person procurement and sourcing team. Earlier employers listed there: **Expeditors International** (freight/logistics), **Neuland Laboratories** and **BioGenex**. So he has a **logistics and supply-chain** background, not marketing. Exact scope (direct vs indirect spend, Canada only vs global) is **to be confirmed** on the call.

company.text: **Sun Pharmaceutical Industries** is India's largest drugmaker, headquartered in **Mumbai**, listed in India. It sells generics, branded specialty medicines and consumer health in 100+ countries. Lead specialty product: **Ilumya** (psoriasis, ~US$796M in FY26). Sun has specialty lines in **dermatology, ophthalmology and onco-dermatology**. In **June 2024** it took **100% ownership of Taro Pharmaceuticals**, a dermatology/topicals specialist with a manufacturing site in **Brampton, Ontario** and a US arm (Taro Pharmaceuticals U.S.A.). In 2026 Sun agreed to acquire **Organon** (women's health, biosimilars, legacy Merck brands; New Jersey based; 2025 sales US$6.2B) for **US$11.75B**, expected to close **by early 2027**. That deal would make Sun a top-10 global biosimilars player and much bigger in North America.

financials.text: **FY26 (year to March 2026):** consolidated revenue **~Rs 58,220 crore**, up ~12% (about US$6.5–7B; conversion is an estimate). EBITDA **~Rs 17,731 crore** (~30% margin). Q4 FY26 net profit up 26% to Rs 2,714 crore. **US = ~29% of sales**; US generics roughly flat; global specialty sales **~US$1.42B**. R&D ~6% of sales. FY27 guidance: mid-to-high single-digit growth. Net cash was ~Rs 30,100 crore before the Organon deal, which will add debt. Canada-only revenue is **not published** (to be confirmed).

history.text: Anne connected with Ramana on LinkedIn. Ramana wrote: "Hello Anne, Good Day!! Can we set up something for Friday morning?" Anne asked for his best email (twice). On **Sep 28** he replied with **ramana.tata@sunpharma.com**. Box created Sep 29 by Johanna T, moved to Contacted Nov 2. **No email sent to him is logged in Streak**, so the Friday meeting he asked for was apparently **never booked** (5 weeks ago). This is the exact stall pattern in the campaign report: yes, then email, then nothing. **Open next step:** Anne emails him now with concrete slots and a calendar link.

industry.title: Procurement under pressure
industry.text: Pharma margins are squeezed (Sun's Q4 margin fell 160 bps on higher R&D and marketing). Procurement teams are asked to cut **indirect spend**: print, promotional materials, events. Supplier consolidation is the usual lever.

industry.title: M&A means supplier rationalisation
industry.text: Sun is merging **Taro** and buying **Organon**. Each integration brings duplicate print vendors, agencies and event suppliers. A single managed print/POS partner across brands is an easy story to tell.

industry.title: Regulated print
industry.text: Pharma print (patient leaflets, HCP materials, pharmacy POS) needs **version control and approvals**. This is where a workflow platform like **Kazaar** (briefs, quotes, approvals, suppliers) adds value beyond price.

industry.title: Trade shows and conferences
industry.text: Dermatology is Taro's core. Medical congresses (e.g. the **AAD Annual Meeting** in the US) and pharmacy shows need booths, pop-ups and printed collateral, often bought ad hoc. Altavia's **pop-up activations for trade shows and conferences** fit here. Sun/Taro's actual event footprint is **to be confirmed**.

talking_points: You asked for a Friday morning: which Friday works, and how long do you have?
What does your team source for Taro Canada today: packaging and inserts, marketing print, pharmacy POS, trade-show material?
Is your scope Canada only, North America, or global as your title suggests?
How many print and POS suppliers do you work with today? Who approves the artwork?
Is the Taro integration, and now Organon, changing your vendor list or approval rules?
Do your brand teams run booths or pop-ups at medical or pharmacy conferences? Who buys those?
Would a short cost review of one category (for example printed materials) be useful as a first step?

attention.title: Five weeks of silence
attention.text: He asked for a meeting on his own and nobody followed up. **Acknowledge it briefly** and make booking effortless.

attention.title: Direct vs indirect spend
attention.text: His background is logistics. He may buy **direct materials** (packaging components, freight) rather than marketing print. Find out early; if so, ask who owns marketing/POS spend and get an introduction.

attention.title: Title not fully verified
attention.text: Streak says "Global ... Lead"; a public org chart says "Specialist" at Taro Canada. Treat his **seniority and budget authority as to be confirmed**.

attention.title: Regulatory sensitivity
attention.text: Do not promise anything that touches GMP packaging or labelling compliance. Position Altavia on **marketing print, POS, events and procurement workflow**.
